summary.approach: Source-first mechanical translation of Stanley J.O. Tinn's readable principles into the supplied reduced educational ornithopter model.

selected_photographs.principle_used: Mute swan span, wrist span proportion, broad inner wing and rounded tapered outer planform basis.
readable_evidence: Rounded 'Say' values: span 7.4 ft and wrist span 3.7 ft = 50% span.
Area paragraph states total area 6.61 ft^2 and AR = b^2/S = 8.29.
uncertain_or_rejected: The 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is inconsistent and was not used.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Scaled to the supplied 14 m full span, giving wing_area_m2 = 14^2 / 8.29.

selected_photographs.principle_used: Section chart treated as qualitative context only, especially for curved-plate outer-wing behaviour.
readable_evidence: Multi-axis Göttingen 417a curved-plate plot suggests high-lift/high-drag qualitative behaviour.
uncertain_or_rejected: Low-Re graph is ambiguous in the photograph and not suitable for direct full-scale digitisation.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Used the supplied illustrative inner/outer section tables from engineering.json instead of inventing recovered coefficients.

selected_photographs.principle_used: Human-carrying ornithopter intent and ideal sine-wave target-trajectory method for required wing forces.
readable_evidence: Text describes defining an ideal trajectory as a sine wave and evaluating candidate wing actions against that requirement.
Text explicitly frames a manned mechanical flapping-flight challenge.
uncertain_or_rejected: No recoverable full design algorithm appendix values are visible here.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Implemented force generation from actual local strip velocities and retained the supplied human-carrying mass/engine reduction.

selected_photographs.principle_used: Straight-and-level flapping is cyclic, with ring-gait context at low speed and powered human-carrying motivation.
readable_evidence: Text says lift and thrust vary cyclically and progress follows an undulating trajectory.
Text mentions further work toward a powered man-carrying ornithopter.
uncertain_or_rejected: The marginal handwritten note is not fully readable.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Model keeps genuinely cyclic wing forces rather than prescribing constant lift or thrust.

selected_photographs.principle_used: Longer downstroke duration at low speed, equal timing in cruise, and wing/body resonance to reduce inertial power.
readable_evidence: Text states low-speed flap-down lasts longer than recovery, tending to equal periods as speed increases.
Text discusses matching required and candidate forces and modelling the wing-wishbone-body assembly as a resonant system.
uncertain_or_rejected: Many handwritten marginal revisions are uncertain.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Implemented timing bias theta = phi - b sin(phi), low-speed default b = 0.3, cruise b = 0, and a coupled spring-inertia solve.

selected_photographs.principle_used: Actual local-force directions from wing motion, fore/aft motion, recovery closing, elastic exchange, and body pitching reaction.
readable_evidence: Text describes wing/body inertias with springiness as a resonant system.
Text says fore and aft wing movement changes the separation between cg and centre of lift, creating oscillating pitching moments.
Wing-action paragraph describes wrist/finger trailing on recovery and working-stroke drag/lift generation.
uncertain_or_rejected: Some handwritten annotations are too faint to recover confidently.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Forces are resolved from body-relative airflow plus actual strip motion; sweep, exposure change and body-pitch coupling are all active in the same dynamics.

selected_photographs.principle_used: Incidence, camber and thickness treated as distinct, with the goshawk figure used only as a generic sectional illustration.
readable_evidence: Opening continuation refers to adjustment of local incidences to optimise thrust and drag.
The page introduces another bird wing and shows different cross-sectional cambers.
uncertain_or_rejected: The goshawk dimensions and listed camber percentages are not taken as swan specifications.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Implemented separate phase-varying twist and camber fields, while thickness stays in the supplied structural metadata.

selected_photographs.principle_used: 5-6% thick inner arm wing, negligible-thickness slotted curved outer hand wing, plus compatibility of conventional tail/rudder controls.
readable_evidence: Text states arm-wing thickness is 5 to 6% and the outer hand wing is effectively a slotted curved plate.
Text says trailing/partial closing on recovery reduces the high-drag outer area.
Text explicitly allows a more conventional tail or weight-shift technique for manoeuvring.
uncertain_or_rejected: Takeoff stroke angles are descriptive rather than a complete numerical mechanism specification.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Used the supplied 0.055 inner and 0.008 outer thickness fractions, sliding overlapping outer leaves, and a conventional tailplane/rudder completion.

selected_photographs.principle_used: Glide D*V baseline work and additional aerodynamic, trajectory and inertial power terms, with spring energy as transfer not free propulsion.
readable_evidence: Text defines base gliding power from drag times speed.
Text lists added power from extra lift/thrust, fore-aft acceleration, cyclic vertical motion and inertial wing motion.
uncertain_or_rejected: No appendix algorithm details are visible on this page.
selected_photographs.engineering_completion: Energy accounting records shaft work, aerodynamic dissipation, damping/transmission heat and pilot control work separately; the spring only stores and returns mechanical energy.

explicit_engineering_assumptions_not_cla: 14 m aircraft span, 55 kg seated pilot, 173.9 kg dry mass and 3.6 kg initial fuel.
16 kW capped engine model, 85% transmission efficiency and reflected drive inertia.
Illustrative inner/outer aerodynamic coefficient tables in engineering.json.
Specific linkage-completion phase curves for stroke, twist, sweep, exposure and camber.
Conventional tricycle landing gear, runway contact reduction and simplified roll/yaw treatment.
limitations: The photographs do not provide a complete validated full-scale aircraft design, stability analysis or structural proof.
Missing appendices, uncertain handwriting and the ambiguous low-Re section chart leave major gaps filled only by the supplied educational engineering model.
The implemented simulation is a reduced strip-and-mass-point model, not CFD, flexible-structure analysis or experimentally validated flight prediction.
